findings.title: Notification text switched from escaped interpolation to [innerHTML], allowing HTML injection from server and remote error strings
findings.problem: Producers pass backend/remote-controlled strings straight into text: server.errorMessage (header.component.ts:49), latestRemoteScanError (header.component.ts:96), bulk result.errorMessage (file-list.component.ts:554), settings reaction.errorMessage (settings-page.component.ts:170,239,257). DomSanitizer keeps and , so a remote file name or scan error renders as a working phishing link or beacon inside a trusted DANGER notification.
findings.fix_hint: Revert to {{ notif.text }}. If one producer (e.g. the version URL) needs a link, add a typed structured field such as linkUrl
findings.why_it_matters: A protection that held for every input is swapped for a library-default sanitizer, across every notification producer including ones relaying remote strings. Violates the CLAUDE.md rule against rendering user-supplied content via innerHTML.

members.title: Plain-text notification messages now parsed as HTML, so text containing < or & gets garbled or dropped
members.problem: Notification.text is a plain string filled by producers that never emit markup (localization.ts, server/remote error strings). [innerHTML] parses them as HTML, so '<...>' segments are stripped and entities decoded; Angular logs sanitizer warnings. Pure regression with no gain.
members.why_it_matters: Server and remote-scan error messages are how users diagnose failures; parts silently disappearing makes them wrong or incomplete.
members.fix_hint: revert to {{ notif.text }} interpolation; if a clickable link is wanted, add a typed link field and render it with <a [href]>

members.title: Remote error output can inject phishing links into notifications
members.problem: After a successful scan, a remote command can fail with output Reconnect your account. sshcp.py:155 carries command output into SshcpError; remote_scanner.py:85-87 wraps it as a recoverable ScannerError; scanner_process.py:90-94 and controller.py:633 propagate it into status. HeaderComponent (header.component.ts:96-108) publishes it as notification text without escaping. The changed binding turns that literal text into a clickable attacker-controlled link; Angular's sanitizer permits anchors and HTTPS hrefs.
members.why_it_matters: Rendering all notification text as HTML enables remote error messages to inject deceptive links.
members.fix_hint: Keep notification text interpolated. If links are needed, represent them as separate validated fields and render explicit anchors. Add a regression test using the real template; the existing bell tests override it with the old interpolation.

members.title: Interpolation replaced with [innerHTML] binding enables HTML/script injection via remote-influenced notification text
members.problem: {{ }} unconditionally escaped; [innerHTML] parses HTML and relies solely on DomSanitizer. notif.text traces to status.server.errorMessage (header.component.ts:49) and latestRemoteScanError via STATUS_REMOTE_SERVER_ERROR (header.component.ts:96, localization.ts:15-16), which is str(e) of a remote scan exception (serialize_status.py:37, controller.py:633, scanner_process.py:94) with no escaping anywhere. Permits markup injection (links, fake buttons, phishing content) today and full XSS on any sanitizer gap or future bypassSecurityTrustHtml.
members.why_it_matters: Text interpolation made injection structurally impossible; safety is now conditional on the sanitizer for content that traces to remote-scan error strings.
members.fix_hint: revert to text interpolation ({{ notif.text }}); if HTML is a genuine requirement, keep interpolation for error/status-derived text and use [innerHTML] only for verified non-remote content

members.title: Notification.text silently changes from a plain-text contract to an HTML contract for every producer
members.problem: Notification.text is typed string (notification.ts:5) and filled by at least 6 producers passing plain text, several from the backend/network. Binding via [innerHTML] changes the field's meaning for all of them; none was updated and the type gives no signal. No producer emits HTML today, so no in-tree consumer needs it.
members.why_it_matters: Moves an escaping duty onto every current and future producer. The codebase's other HTML sink (confirm-modal.service.ts) escapes every field before innerHTML; this sink skips that.
members.fix_hint: revert to {{ notif.text }}; if a link is needed, add a typed field such as link?: {href, label} to Notification and render it with a template anchor

members.title: Plain-text error messages containing < or & are now mangled or silently dropped
members.problem: Every producer builds plain text. With innerHTML a remote scan error like 'bash: <stdin>: line 1: syntax error', a file name like 'Tom & Jerry <1080p>.mkv', or a validation message like 'expected <host:port>' is parsed as markup: tag-like pieces vanish and entities decode, so users see incomplete or misleading errors.
members.why_it_matters: Error notifications are how users diagnose remote-connection and bulk-action failures.
members.fix_hint: Keep text interpolation; the producers emit plain text

members.title: Removing output escaping opens HTML/markup injection from remote-server error text into the notification bell
members.problem: The new [innerHTML] binding relies only on Angular's DomSanitizer, which still allows , and formatting. latestRemoteScanError and server.errorMessage reach the bell unescaped (header.component.ts:49,96). The repo elsewhere escapes before innerHTML (confirm-modal.service.ts:33).
members.why_it_matters: Protection now depends on the sanitizer allowlist, which still permits links and images to arbitrary URLs.
members.fix_hint: keep text interpolation ({{ }}); never bind server/remote-originated strings via [innerHTML]
